top_cited_works.title: Nanostructured Copper Interfaces for Enhanced Boiling
top_cited_works.abstract: On the boil: Nanostructured Cu interfaces display enhanced boiling performance at low superheated temperatures compared to untreated Cu, caused by a large increase in the density of active bubble nucleation sites. The enhancement is caused by nanobubbles, which percolate through the interconnected network of nanopores and enable stable nucleation of bubbles at microscale cavities (defects) on the film surface (see picture).

top_cited_works.title: Suppression of Boiling Flow Oscillations in Parallel Microchannels by Inlet Restrictors
top_cited_works.venue: ASME Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
top_cited_works.abstract: Geometrical effects of MEMS-based microfabricated inlet orifices on the suppression of parallel channel and upstream compressible volume instabilities commonly exhibited during flow boiling in parallel microchannels have been investigated. The heat fluxes at the onset of unstable boiling have been obtained over effective heat fluxes ranging from 9 to 614W∕cm2 and mass fluxes from 115to389kg∕m2s. A dimensionless parameter M, which accounts for the pressure drop increase imposed by the inlet restrictors, has been used to correlate the extent of flow instability suppression. It has been shown that the onset of unstable boiling asymptotically increases with M. At sufficiently high M values, parallel channels and upstream compressible volume instabilities are completely eradicated although it gives way to another instability to develop, namely, the critical heat flux conditions. A correlation has been developed in terms of M to predict the conditions leading to unstable boiling.

recent_works.title: Experimental demonstration of liquid CO2 flow dynamics using backlight PIV
Flow Boiling of an Array of Impinging CO 2 Micro-Jets near Critical Conditions
recent_works.abstract: An experimental study about flow boiling of multiple micro-jets of CO2 at high reduced pressures was conducted. A micro device with a serpentine-shaped heater and three concentrically arranged resistive temperature detectors was micro-fabricated and used in conjunction with conventionally machined 13 micro jets perpendicular to them, each with a diameter of 206 µm, with the inter-jet separation being ∼1.5 and a relative standoff of ∼7.3. The device was placed in a custom-made package that connected the flow and electronic circuit to the outside environment. Mass flux values ranged from 880 to 2360 kg/m2.s, pressure ranged from 5.86 to 6.895 MPa (i.e., reduced pressures from 0.794 to 0.934), and heat flux ranged from 3 to 58 W/cm2. The inlet conditions of the experiments were tailored to be at a temperature around 21–24 °C, closer to the saturation temperatures of the intended experimental pressure, to bring about the rapid onset of nucleate boiling (ONB). The experimental results entailed that the boiling curves, heat transfer coefficients (HTC), and critical heat flux (CHF) were all influenced by radial position, heat flux, mass flux, and pressure. recent_works.title: Two-phase choked flow of trans critical carbon dioxide at the micro scale
recent_works.abstract: An experimental study about two-phase carbon dioxide (CO2) choking flow inside parallel microchannels with hydraulic diameters of 66.6 μm is conducted. Trans critical CO2 with a reduced pressure ranging from 0.9 to 1.1 (i.e., from 6.5 to 8 MPa) is introduced at the inlet and is exhausted downstream at a reduced outlet pressure ranging from 0.135 to 1.016 (i.e., from 1 to 7.5 MPa). Mass flow rates as a function of pressure drop are obtained, and choking conditions are determined. Subsequently, the vapor and liquid velocities are inferred using the thermodynamic properties of the flow and several void fraction models. The speed of sound of the vapor, the liquid, and the mixture are calculated based on the homogenous flow model, slug flow model, and stratified flow model. All void fraction models that are examined predict the vapor Mach number at the onset of choking somewhere below unity. The stratified flow model provides a more accurate prediction of the experimentally obtained flow choking, indicating that the liquid achieves its effective sonic velocity well before the vapor and is therefore conjectured to control flow choking.
